seo.title: Smart Wallet for Men in Pakistan — RFID Slim Leather | Kordovan
seo.description: Smart wallets for men in Pakistan: slim RFID-blocking leather card holders and pop-up wallets. Handmade in our own workshop, cash on delivery available.

ed.value:
Smart Wallets for Men in Pakistan

Slim should not mean giving anything up. A smart wallet trades the two folds of a traditional bifold for a mechanism — a pull-strap, an elastic band or a pop-up card stack — that presents your cards in one motion and holds them in a fraction of the thickness. Ours pair that engineering with genuine leather, so the thing lasting ten years is the leather, not the gimmick.

What "RFID protected" actually does

Contactless debit and credit cards answer any reader that comes within a few centimetres. An RFID-blocking wallet carries a thin metallic layer that detunes that signal, so the card cannot be read through the wallet. It is a small risk in Pakistan today and a growing one as contactless spreads — the point is that it costs nothing to have, and cannot be added later.

Choosing between them

  • Pop-up card wallet — press the lever and the cards fan out in order. Fastest access, holds six to eight cards, the closest thing to a traditional wallet in slim form.
  • Vertical pull-strap — cards stack flat and the strap lifts them together. The slimmest option, and the best for a front pocket.
  • Card holder — no mechanism at all, just leather sleeves. Three to five cards and a folded note, and nothing to break.
  • Magic wallet — the ribbon fold that flips notes from either side. Genuinely thin, and the most fun to use.

What they cost

Our smart wallets run Rs 1,800 to Rs 3,200. Below roughly Rs 1,200 you are buying a metal cage with a PU wrap, and the wrap fails long before the cage does. The KODO — Pakistan's first RFID-protected leather smart wallet — sits in the middle of our range.

How many cards do you actually carry?

The honest answer is usually four to six, and most people buy a wallet sized for twelve. A smart wallet is worth it only if you commit to carrying what you use; if you need a receipt pocket and room for cash, a traditional leather bifold is the better buy and we will say so.

Every wallet carries a lifetime craftsmanship warranty. Cash on delivery is available, and delivery is free on orders over Rs 5,500.

seo.title: Leather Jacket Price in Pakistan: Rs 22,000 to 35,000
seo.description: Original men's leather jacket prices in Pakistan: Rs 22,000–35,000. Each cut in your size for one customer, so paid online; about 3 weeks to your door.

ed.value:
Buying men's leather jackets in Pakistan

Every jacket on this page is made to order in Pakistan. We hold no finished stock, so yours is cut in your size, for you, after you check out. Production takes time, and that is the trade we have chosen: fit is the one thing a leather jacket cannot fake.

Leather jacket price in Pakistan

Our men's leather jackets cost Rs 22,000 to Rs 35,000 at regular price, the honest range for a genuine sheepskin jacket made in Pakistan. Here is how they divide.

  • Rs 22,000 to 25,999. Our simplest patterns: The Iconic and the Sheppard cafe racer.
  • Rs 26,000 to 29,999. More panels, quilting, bomber trims and waxed or vintage finishes: Alonzo, The Ace, Rodriguez.
  • Rs 30,000 to 35,000. The top of the range: Desert Voyager, the double-breasted Hawkeye, Urban Rider.

What drives the price

  • The grade of hide. Full-grain keeps the whole outer surface; top-grain is lightly corrected for an even finish. "Genuine leather" on a label is a grade name, often split hide, the weaker under-layer. Every jacket here is top-grain sheepskin, lighter and softer than cowhide.
  • How much hide. Longer cuts, quilting and double-breasted fronts use more of it.
  • Lining, stitching and zips. The parts you notice in the second winter.

What leather jackets cost across Pakistan

  • Under Rs 8,000: almost always PU, rexine or bonded leather. The hide alone costs more than that.
  • Rs 8,000 to 15,000: a blend, a thin hide, or a genuine jacket on heavy discount. Ask what the shell is.
  • Rs 20,000 to 40,000: the honest band for a full genuine leather jacket made locally.
  • Above Rs 45,000: usually imported or a designer margin, not necessarily better leather.

Bands are indicative; other brands' prices change weekly, so we do not quote them.

Real leather or rexine: three checks

  • Pores. Irregular on real hide; repeating on rexine, which is printed from a roll.
  • Press it. Leather creases and springs back. Rexine stays flat and uniform.
  • The cut edge. Inside a pocket or under the hem, leather shows a fibrous underside. Rexine shows a fabric backing.

Why jackets are paid online, and how long they take

Each jacket is cut for one customer, in your size, and cannot be resold if refused at the door. That is why it is paid in full online (card or JazzCash) and cash on delivery is not offered. Allow about 3 weeks to your door; winter is our busiest season, and we would rather quote honestly than promise a date we cannot hold. Delivery is free.

Still comparing brands? Our guide to the top 10 leather jacket brands in Pakistan sets these bands against ten labels, ours included.

Choosing your cut

Biker jackets have the asymmetric zip and belted waist — the most structured shape here, and the most casual. Bombers use a ribbed collar, cuff and hem, which makes them the most forgiving to wear and the easiest to size. Cafe racers are minimal, with a band collar and a straight centre zip; they are the only cut in the range that sits comfortably over a shirt. Vintage and distressed finishes arrive already broken in, and hide everyday scuffing better than a clean finish does.

Looking for one colour in particular? See every black leather jacket across all three cuts.

Getting the size right

The most common mistake is buying for September and wearing in January. Order to the measurement chart rather than your usual shirt size, and if you are in Lahore, Islamabad, Rawalpindi or anywhere further north, allow room across the chest for a sweater underneath. In the south, around Hyderabad and the coast, a lined jacket on its own carries most of the season, so a closer fit works.

Leather jacket prices: common questions

What is the price of an original leather jacket in Pakistan?

A genuine leather jacket made in Pakistan costs roughly Rs 20,000 to Rs 40,000. Ours run from Rs 22,000 to Rs 35,000 at regular price, all in top-grain sheepskin.

Why are some leather jackets so cheap?

Below about Rs 8,000 a jacket is almost always PU, rexine or bonded leather, because the hide for a full jacket costs more than that before any cutting or stitching.

How can I tell a real leather jacket from rexine?

Check three things: irregular pores (rexine repeats), a surface that creases and springs back when pressed, and a fibrous, suede-like underside at a cut edge instead of a fabric backing.

Is a sheep leather jacket cheaper than cow leather?

Not by rule. Price follows the grade and the amount of hide more than the animal. Sheepskin is lighter and softer; cowhide is heavier and tougher. Every jacket on this page is sheepskin; any style can also be made in cowhide, priced separately, if you ask us on WhatsApp.

Why are your jackets paid online, and how long is delivery?

Each jacket is cut for one customer in your size and cannot be resold, so it is paid in full online and cash on delivery is not offered. Allow about 3 weeks to your door; winter is our busiest season. Delivery is free.

Leather Jackets for Women in Pakistan

Most women's leather jackets sold here are men's patterns scaled down, which is why they so often sit wrong at the shoulder and the waist. Ours are cut to their own pattern, in semi-aniline sheep leather — a lighter, softer hide than the cowhide used for men's outerwear, finished with minimal pigment so the natural grain still shows through.

How it should fit

The shoulder seam is the one measurement that cannot be corrected later: it should land on the edge of your shoulder, not past it. Everything else follows from there. Because each jacket is made to order, tell us how you intend to wear it — a jacket meant to close over a knit through an Islamabad winter needs different room across the chest than one worn open over a shirt on the coast.

Caring for a lighter hide

Semi-aniline leather is more breathable and more supple than a heavily pigmented finish, and slightly more open to marking as a result. That is the trade for a jacket that actually feels like leather rather than like a coating. Keep it out of prolonged direct sun, let it dry naturally if it gets wet, and condition it once a season.

How to choose a wallet for men: styles, leathers and prices explained

Which wallet for men suits the way you carry?

Start with your pocket, not the wallet. A wallet that's too fat for where you keep it either gets left at home or ruins the line of your trousers. Here is how our range breaks down.

  • Classic bifold, Rs 2,400 to Rs 6,200. Cards on both sides, a full-width cash pocket and usually an ID window. The right wallet if you carry notes and six to twelve cards. Our best-seller, the Mocha Mate, adds an outer coin pocket. The Bastion has a distressed finish that shrugs off daily scuffs.
  • Slim wallet, Rs 1,499 to Rs 4,200. Soft sheep leather that sits flat in a front pocket. The Rigor Lite takes ten cards and two lots of notes for Rs 1,499.
  • Card holder or money clip, Rs 1,800 to Rs 6,250. For the man who carries a handful of cards and a few folded notes. Try the Elite Card Holder or The Money Clip.
  • Long and mobile wallets, Rs 3,900 to Rs 4,500. Notes lie flat without folding, and some take your phone too. See the Crazy Horse Long and The Elite.
  • Smart and RFID wallets. A shielded lining keeps contactless cards unreadable to skimmers. Browse smart wallets for men.

Which leather should you pick?

  • Full-grain cow leather is the toughest. It darkens and softens with use, so a two-year-old wallet looks better than a new one.
  • Crazy horse leather is waxed. Scratches burnish back into the surface instead of showing white. The Bronco and Truckkr are made from it.
  • Nappa is smooth and supple from the first day, and it suits a suit. See the Plain Bifold.
  • Sheep leather is the lightest and thinnest, which is why our slim wallets use it.
  • Saffiano has a cross-hatch pressed into it, so it resists scratches and keeps its colour. See the Premium Saffiano.

Real leather or PU?

A lot of cheap wallets sold online in Pakistan are PU or bonded leather with "leather" in the title. Real leather has an irregular grain, a fibrous cut edge and a smell of tannery, and it gets better with age. PU peels at the fold, usually within a year. Our full checklist: real vs fake leather, 8 ways to check before you buy.

Common questions

How much does a genuine leather wallet cost in Pakistan?

A genuine leather wallet made locally starts around Rs 1,500 for a slim sheep leather piece and runs past Rs 6,000 for crazy horse and hand-stitched work. Ours run from Rs 1,499 to Rs 6,500.

Can I pay cash on delivery?

Yes. Cash on delivery is available on wallets anywhere in Pakistan.

What does the lifetime warranty cover?

If the stitching or hardware fails in normal use, we repair or replace the wallet.

Which wallet makes the best gift?

For weddings and Eid, a classic bifold like the Mocha Mate or Shelby & Thomas suits almost anyone. For something boxed and ready to give, see our leather gift sets.

Still comparing brands? Read our guide to the top 10 leather wallet brands in Pakistan.

Leather Wallets for Men in Pakistan

A wallet is the one piece of leather you reach for every single day, so it is the one that shows whether you bought well. Ours are made in Pakistan from full-grain, nappa and crazy horse hide — leathers that do not merely survive daily carry but improve with it, darkening at the fold and along the edge into a patina that is yours alone.

Leather wallet price in Pakistan

Our men's wallets cost Rs 1,499 to Rs 6,500 at regular price, inside the honest band for a genuine leather wallet made in Pakistan.

  • Rs 1,499 to 2,499. Slim sheep leather and minimal card carry: Rigor Lite, the full-grain Luke, the nappa Plain Bifold.
  • Rs 2,500 to 3,999. Everyday bifolds in cow and crazy horse leather: The Bastion, Mocha Mate, the crazy horse Truckkr.
  • Rs 4,000 to 6,500. More leather, more hand work: The Armour, Bronco, the handwoven full-grain Stallion.

Our RFID wallets, the KODO and The Razor, sit at Rs 2,300 to Rs 2,450; see the smart wallet range.

What drives the price

  • Which layer of the hide. Full-grain keeps the outer surface and develops a patina; top-grain is sanded even. "Genuine leather" is a grade name, often split hide.
  • Which leather. Cow is toughest, crazy horse is waxed so scratches burnish back, nappa is soft from day one, sheep is thinnest.
  • Stitching and slots. The fold and card slots fail first on a cheap wallet. Tight, even stitching is where the money goes.
  • RFID and hardware. A shielded lining, zip or clip adds cost.

What leather wallets cost across Pakistan

  • Under Rs 800: almost certainly PU, rexine or bonded leather. It cracks along the fold, usually within a year.
  • Rs 800 to 1,500: a blend, a thin split hide, or genuine leather on heavy discount. Ask what the outer material is.
  • Rs 1,500 to 7,000: the honest band for a genuine leather wallet made locally.
  • Above Rs 12,000: usually an imported label, not better hide.

Bands are indicative; other brands' prices change weekly, so we do not quote them.

Real leather or PU: three checks

  • Press it. Leather creases and springs back; PU stays flat.
  • Look at the pores. Irregular on hide, repeating on printed PU.
  • Look inside a card slot. A fibrous, suede-like cut edge, not a fabric mesh.

Wallets are ready-made and dispatched from stock, so cash on delivery is available (Rs 250 more), along with card and JazzCash. Delivery is free on orders over Rs 5,500 paid online.

Comparing brands? Read our guide to the top 10 leather wallet brands in Pakistan.

Which wallet suits how you carry

  • Bifold — the default, and still the best for cash plus six to eight cards. Try the Bastion or the Mocha Mate.
  • Slim and minimalist — front-pocket carry, three to five cards, no bulk against the hip. See the smart wallet range, including RFID-protected options.
  • Long wallet — notes flat and unfolded, which is how currency lasts. The right choice if you carry cash daily.
  • Card holder and money clip — cards and a folded note, nothing else. The smallest thing that still does the job.

Care, and how long it should last

A full-grain wallet should outlast a decade of daily use. Keep it out of a back pocket you sit on — the constant flex, not age, is what kills stitching — and condition it lightly once or twice a year. It will get darker and softer, and that is the leather working correctly, not wearing out.

Every Kordovan wallet carries a lifetime craftsmanship warranty: if stitching or hardware fails in normal use, we repair or replace it.

Leather wallet prices: common questions

What is the price of a genuine leather wallet in Pakistan?

A genuine leather wallet made in Pakistan costs roughly Rs 1,500 to Rs 7,000. Ours run from Rs 1,499 to Rs 6,500 at regular price, depending on the leather and how much hand work goes into it.

Why are some leather wallets under Rs 1,000?

Below about Rs 800 a wallet is almost always PU, rexine or bonded leather. It looks right for a season, then cracks along the fold, because that is where a coating fails first.

Is a cow leather wallet better than sheep leather?

Cow leather is tougher and darkens well with use, so it suits a bifold you carry daily. Sheep leather is thinner and lighter, which is why our slimmest wallets, such as the Rigor Lite, use it.

How much does an RFID wallet cost, and do I need one?

Our RFID wallets, the KODO and The Razor, are Rs 2,300 to Rs 2,450. RFID shielding only matters if you carry contactless cards; with chip-and-PIN cards alone, it does nothing for you.

Can I pay cash on delivery for a wallet?

Yes. Wallets are ready-made and dispatched from stock, so cash on delivery is available (Rs 250 more), as well as card and JazzCash. Delivery is free on orders over Rs 5,500 paid online.

nodes.descriptionHtml:
Genuine sheep leather gloves for Pakistani winters, at Rs 1,950 a pair. Soft fleece lining for warmth, a non-slip palm for the steering wheel or bike handle, and an adjustable wrist strap so they sit right. Men's in brown and black, women's in dark red, sizes S to 2XL, with cash on delivery across Pakistan.

Leather gloves buying guide: sizes, care and what to wear them with

Why sheep leather gloves for winter?

Sheep leather is thin, supple and warm. It moves with your fingers from the first day instead of fighting them like thick cowhide, so you can still grip a steering wheel, pull a key from your pocket or hold a bike throttle. Ours pair that leather with a spandex palm panel for stretch and a soft fleece lining that holds heat on foggy mornings and night rides.

Which pair is right for you?

  • Men's sheep leather winter gloves in brown: our most-bought pair. Warm tan leather that ages into a deeper colour and goes with denim, a bomber or a camel coat.
  • Men's sheep leather winter gloves in black: the sharper choice for office wear, a black leather jacket or a formal shalwar kameez with a waistcoat.
  • Women's sheep leather winter gloves in dark red: a slimmer cut in a rich colour that lifts a black coat or shawl.

Are these good bike gloves?

For everyday riding to work or university, yes. The non-slip palm patch keeps a firm hold on the handle, the strap stops cold air getting in at the wrist, and leather cuts the wind far better than wool or knitted gloves. They are winter riding gloves, not armoured racing gloves.

How do I pick my size?

Every pair comes in S, M, L, XL and 2XL. Most men wear M or L, and most women S or M. Leather gloves should feel snug on day one; they relax slightly with wear and the wrist strap takes up any slack. If you are between sizes and plan to ride, take the smaller one.

How do I care for leather gloves?

Let them dry naturally if they get wet, away from a heater, then flex them gently. Wipe with a slightly damp cloth, and condition the leather once or twice a season. Store them flat, not balled up in a pocket, and a good pair will see you through many winters.

Common questions

What is the price of leather gloves in Pakistan?

Prices for leather gloves in Pakistan vary a lot, and the cheapest are rarely real leather. Kordovan's fleece-lined sheep leather gloves are Rs 1,950 for every colour and size. PU "leather" gloves look similar on the shelf but crack and stop keeping you warm within a season. Our guide on leather brands in Pakistan explains what to look for.

Can I pay cash on delivery?

Yes, cash on delivery is available across Pakistan, and delivery is free on orders over Rs 5,500. Adding gloves to a jacket or wallet order is the easiest way to get there.

Do leather gloves make a good gift?

They are one of the most practical winter gifts there is, for wedding season or a birthday. Pair them with a leather wallet or browse our gift sets.

Complete your winter look

Gloves are only half the story. See our men's leather jackets, leather caps and our guide to the best winter jackets in Pakistan.

seo.title: Leather Office Bags & Briefcases for Men in Pakistan | Kordovan
seo.description: Genuine leather office bags and briefcases in Pakistan. Structured, laptop-ready and hand-stitched in our own workshop. Free delivery over PKR 5,500.

ed.value:
Leather Office Bags and Briefcases in Pakistan

An office bag is worn, not used — it is in the room before you say anything. That is why we build these structured rather than slouchy, from full-grain hide that holds its shape when it is set down on a boardroom floor and keeps holding it after five years of the same journey.

What a leather briefcase costs in Pakistan

This is the question most people arrive with, so here is the straight answer.

  • Under Rs 5,000 — PU or bonded leather over a board frame. It photographs like a briefcase and it delaminates at the corners within a year or two.
  • Rs 5,000 – 15,000 — split leather, or genuine leather panels over synthetic gussets. Real hide somewhere in it, but usually not where the wear happens.
  • Rs 17,000 – 42,000 — where our range sits, and where a full-grain briefcase built to last a career begins. The hide, the lining, the frame and the hardware all cost real money at this size, because a briefcase uses four to six times the leather a wallet does.

Ours run Rs 17,600 to Rs 42,000, from the Documate with its code lock up to the CEO Executive and the Staton in premium cow leather.

What separates a work bag from a weekend bag

  • It holds shape empty. A soft bag looks unprepared in a meeting. Structure comes from the leather weight and the panel construction, not from a stiffener that later cracks.
  • Documents fit flat. A4 and legal-size papers should slide in without bending — the most common failure on bags designed to a photograph rather than a use.
  • A padded laptop section, separate from the document space, so a metal edge is not resting against paperwork.
  • A handle and a strap. Carried by hand into the office, worn across the body on the commute.

Colour

Black is the safe formal answer and hides scuffs longest. Brown and tan are warmer, age more visibly, and now read as perfectly acceptable business colours in Pakistan — a brown bag with a navy or grey suit is a deliberate choice, not a mistake.

Also see our leather laptop bags for messenger and backpack shapes, or the full leather bags range. Every piece carries a lifetime craftsmanship warranty. Free delivery on orders over Rs 5,500, cash on delivery available.

seo.title: Leather Laptop Bags in Pakistan — 13", 14" & 15.6" | Kordovan
seo.description: Genuine leather laptop bags and messenger bags in Pakistan, padded for 13-15.6 inch machines. Hand-stitched in our own workshop. Free delivery over PKR 5,500.

ed.value:
Leather Laptop Bags in Pakistan

A laptop bag has one job before it has any others: the machine has to survive the day. That means a padded sleeve that actually fits, a base that does not sag, and stitching at the strap anchors that will hold three kilos for years rather than months.

Getting the size right

Laptop sizes are measured across the screen diagonal, not the body, so a 15.6-inch machine is roughly 36 x 25 cm and a 13-inch is roughly 30 x 21 cm. Buy a bag rated at or just above your screen size — a sleeve that is too big lets the machine slide, which is how corners get damaged.

  • 13-inch and 14-inch — MacBook Air and most ultrabooks. A slim briefcase or messenger carries these comfortably.
  • 15.6-inch — the standard Windows work laptop and most gaming machines. Needs a fuller-bodied bag, and the charger takes real space.

We also make slim sleeves in three sizes from Rs 8,500 if you already have a bag and only need to protect the machine inside it.

Briefcase, messenger or backpack?

A briefcase reads formal, holds shape when set down, and is the right call for client meetings — see the office bag range. A messenger is worn across the body, opens faster, and suits a commute where the bag is on and off all day. A backpack spreads the weight across both shoulders, which matters more than people expect once a charger and a water bottle go in beside the laptop. All three hold the same machine — the difference is how you carry it and how you want to look carrying it.

What it costs

ed.value:
Leather Travel Bags in Pakistan

A travel bag gets treated worse than anything else you own. It is thrown into car boots, dragged across airport floors and packed past the point the maker intended. That is why we build these from full-grain and crazy horse hide rather than the thinner splits used on fashion luggage — the marks it picks up become the finish rather than the damage.

What to check before you buy one

  • Cabin size. Most Pakistani carriers allow roughly 55 x 35 x 25 cm for hand luggage. Measure the bag, not the description — a soft duffle packed full is larger than its stated size.
  • The base. Reinforced corners or metal feet are what stop a bag wearing through where it is set down. This is the first thing to fail on a cheap duffle.
  • Strap anchors. Where the shoulder strap meets the body carries the entire loaded weight. Riveted or double-stitched anchors last; a single line of stitching does not.
  • Zip quality. A full-length zip that fails ends the bag, because replacing one costs more than most people will pay.

Every Kordovan bag carries a lifetime craftsmanship warranty on stitching and hardware in normal use. Free delivery over PKR 5,500, and cash on delivery is available on all ready-made pieces.

ed.value:
Leather Caps for Men in Pakistan

A leather cap is one of the few accessories that genuinely improves with age. Sheep leather is light enough to wear in coastal heat and soft enough that it takes the shape of your head rather than sitting on it — which is why we use it rather than the stiffer cowhide most caps are cut from.

Baseball or flat cap?

  • Baseball cap — adjustable at the back, structured crown, curved peak. Casual, and the more forgiving of the two on fit.
  • Flat cap (newsboy) — softer, rounder, sits closer to the head. Reads smarter, and works with a jacket in a way a baseball cap does not.

Caring for it

Keep it out of direct sun for long periods — heat dries leather out faster than wear does. If it gets wet, let it dry away from heat rather than on a radiator, and stuff the crown so it holds shape. Condition it once or twice a year and it will outlast every fabric cap you own.

ed.value:
Leather Bags in Pakistan

From the desk to the departure gate, a good leather bag carries more than your things — it carries how you show up. Everything on this page is cut and hand-stitched in our own workshop from full-grain and crazy horse hide, and built around real compartments and hardware that lasts rather than around a photograph.

Find the right bag faster

  • Leather laptop bags — padded sleeves sized for 13", 14" and 15.6" machines, in messenger, briefcase and backpack shapes. Rs 12,000 to Rs 42,000, plus slim sleeves from Rs 8,500.
  • Leather office bags and briefcases — structured, A4-flat, laptop-ready. Rs 17,600 to Rs 42,000.
  • Leather travel bags and duffles — weekenders and cabin trolleys built for repeat trips. Rs 29,000 to Rs 45,000.
  • Leather bags for women — totes, cross-body bags and clutches. Rs 6,000 to Rs 19,500.

What separates a leather bag that lasts

Three things fail first on a cheap bag, and all three are visible before you buy. The strap anchors carry the entire loaded weight, so they need rivets or double stitching, not a single line. The base is where a bag wears through, because it is what the bag is set down on — look for reinforced corners or metal feet. The zip ends the bag when it goes, since replacing a full-length zip costs more than most people will spend. Everything else is recoverable; those three are not.

Full-grain or crazy horse?

Full-grain keeps the outermost layer of the hide intact, which is the densest and most durable part, and it darkens evenly with use. Crazy horse is full-grain treated with a heavy wax: it marks readily and the marks rub back out, so it develops a deliberately weathered surface. Neither is better — full-grain suits a formal bag, crazy horse suits one that will be thrown into car boots.

ed.value:
How to get the size right

Hat sizing is the one thing people get wrong buying online, and it is easy to get right. Run a tape measure around your head about a centimetre above your ears and across the middle of your forehead — where the hat will actually sit. Keep it snug, not tight. That measurement in inches is your size:

  • S — 20 to 21.5 inches
  • M — 21.5 to 22.5 inches
  • L — 22.5 to 23 inches
  • XL — 23 inches and above

If you fall between two sizes, take the larger one. Leather gives a little with wear; it does not shrink back.

Which style suits you

  • Crushable — soft, packable leather that springs back into shape. The one to buy if it will live in a car or a bag.
  • Suede — matte, softer surface and a quieter finish. Less shine, more texture.
  • Studded band — a firmer crown with a metal-studded band. The statement piece of the range.
  • Clifford — our heaviest build, in faded black and rustic brown, with a shaped brim that holds its curve.

What a leather cowboy hat should cost in Pakistan

Below about Rs 2,500 you are almost always looking at pressed felt, PU or a coated fabric rather than hide. A genuine leather hat starts around Rs 4,500 and runs to roughly Rs 12,000 depending on the weight of the leather and the hardware. Ours sit inside that band because we make them ourselves rather than import them.

Looking after it

Keep it crown-down on a flat surface or on a hat rack — resting it on the brim will flatten the curve over time. If it gets wet, let it dry away from direct heat and reshape it while it is still slightly damp. A light leather conditioner once or twice a year keeps the hide supple in dry weather.

Visit our shop

You are welcome to try hats on in person at our shop in Malir Cantt — sizing is much easier in the hand than off a chart. Elsewhere in Pakistan we ship with cash on delivery.

Also see our leather caps and the rest of our leather accessories.

ed.value:
The biker jacket, and who it suits

The asymmetric zip is not styling for its own sake. It came from motorcycling, where a centre zip pressed into the sternum as a rider leaned forward, and offsetting it moved the hardware off the breastbone. The belted waist did the same job against wind. Both survived into fashion because they also happen to flatter — the diagonal line across the chest broadens the shoulders and narrows the waist.

How it should fit

Closer than you think. A biker jacket is meant to sit near the body, ending at the hip bone rather than below it, with the shoulder seam landing on the edge of your shoulder and not past it. Sleeves should stop at the wrist bone. If you plan to wear a sweater underneath through a northern winter, order with that layer in mind rather than sizing up afterwards — made to order means the chest can allow for it without ruining the line everywhere else.

Black or brown

Black reads sharper and more formal, and it is the safer first jacket. Brown softens with age more visibly and sits better against denim and earth tones. Distressed and vintage finishes fall between the two: they arrive already broken in, and they hide the scuffing that a clean black finish would show. See all black leather jackets, or the full range of men's leather jackets in Pakistan.

Every biker jacket here is made to order in genuine full-grain sheepskin, and paid in full online at checkout by card or JazzCash — each one is cut for a single customer and can never be resold. Allow about three weeks from checkout to your door; winter is our busiest season and the bench is full. Free delivery nationwide and a lifetime craftsmanship warranty. Prefer something less structured? Look at bomber jackets.

ed.value:
The bomber jacket, and who it suits

The ribbed collar, cuffs and hem are the whole design. They seal the jacket at three points, which is why the shape began as flight clothing, and they are also what makes it the most forgiving cut in leather — the rib takes up slack, so a bomber tolerates a range of body shapes that a structured biker jacket does not.

How it should fit

Roomier than a biker, deliberately. The hem rib should sit at your waistband without riding up, and there should be enough room across the chest to close it over a knit. If the ribbing pulls when you zip it, the jacket is too small — the rib is doing work it was never meant to do.

Where it works

A bomber is the easiest leather jacket to wear with everything, which is exactly why it is the one to buy if you will only own one. It reads casual without reading aggressive, sits well over a t-shirt or a jumper, and does not fight tailored trousers the way a belted biker jacket does. For something with more presence, look at biker jackets; for the black options across every cut, see black leather jackets.

ed.value:
Buying a black leather jacket in Pakistan

Black is the jacket most people buy first, and usually the right call. It is the most forgiving colour to build an outfit around, it reads sharper than brown after dark, and it does not date. The trade is that black shows dust and scuffing more plainly than brown or a distressed finish does, so it rewards a little care.

Not all black is the same

A plain smooth black is the sharpest and the most formal. Waxed and quilted blacks carry texture that catches the light and read less severe. A suede hybrid softens it further again. All three are on this page, across biker, bomber and cafe racer cuts — which means the real decision is shape first, finish second.

Telling real black leather from PU

Black is the colour synthetic imitates best, because a uniform dark finish hides the repeating grain that gives it away. Look at the pores under good light: genuine hide is irregular, and no two patches match. Press it — real leather creases and springs back, and the tone shifts slightly as it stretches.
